The filter that decides whether a scan is usable (water-rich). To be a fair test it must meet three conditions:

1. **Blind.** It uses only the scan itself, never the breast's label or the result of the comparison.
2. **Symmetric.** It is applied the same way to both breasts, so neither is favoured.
3. **The same on every patient.** The threshold is not tuned patient by patient. It was, however, chosen by looking at the sensitivity curve on
   this same set of patients (@fig-on-the-fly), so the headline result is not independent of that choice.

Each breast is scanned a few times, usually three, and some of those scans will miss the glandular tissue. So the rule works scan by scan:

- **A scan is usable** if it has a real water peak: its water peak height (the mean of its prepared curve over q = 20-22) is at least
  **`{python} f"{WATER_MIN:g}"`**, that is `{python} f"{100 * WATER_MIN:.0f}"`% of the fat peak's height, and its fitted water Gaussian is centred at
  **q ≥ `{python} f"{CENTRE_MIN:g}"`**, so the fit has found a water peak and not just the shoulder of the fat peak.
- **A breast is usable** if at least one of its scans is; its Water:Fat comes from the mean of its usable scans only.
- **A patient is compared** only if **both** breasts are usable.

```{python}
#| label: fig-on-the-fly-example
#| fig-cap: "The rule on three breasts. **Left and middle**: one CANCER/NORMAL patient, each breast with usable scans (coloured) and rejected scans (grey dashed); fat (yellow) and water (blue) Gaussians fitted to the mean of the usable scans, with their sum (red dashed). **Right**: a breast with no usable scan — every scan sits below the threshold (black bar over q 20-22), so the breast is not used."
found = rule_breasts(WATER_MIN, CENTRE_MIN)
# usable example: the first CANCER/NORMAL patient with both usable and rejected scans in each breast
example_nova = next(n for n in analysis_novas
                    if (n, "LEFT") in found and (n, "RIGHT") in found
                    and sorted(found[n, s][0] for s in ("LEFT", "RIGHT")) == ["CANCER", "NORMAL"]
                    and all(0 < found[n, s][2] < found[n, s][3] for s in ("LEFT", "RIGHT")))
# not-usable example: a breast with scans but none that pass the rule
rejected_example = next((nova, side, label)
                        for nova, side, label, curve, height, centre in scan_records
                        if label in COHORTS and (nova, side) not in found
                        and sum(1 for n, s, *_ in scan_records if n == nova and s == side) >= 2)

def plot_breast(ax, nova, side, show_fit):
    records = [(label, curve, height, centre, usable(height, centre, WATER_MIN, CENTRE_MIN))
               for n, s, label, curve, height, centre in scan_records if n == nova and s == side]
    label = records[0][0]
    good = []
    for k, (_, curve, height, centre, ok) in enumerate(records):
        tag = f"scan {k + 1}: water {height:.2f}, centre {centre:.1f}"
        if ok:
            good.append(curve)
            ax.plot(q, curve, color=ne.STATUS_COLOURS[label], lw=0.9, label=f"{tag}, usable")
        else:
            ax.plot(q, curve, color="grey", lw=0.8, ls="--", label=f"{tag}, rejected")
    ax.hlines(WATER_MIN, *WATER, color="black", lw=2.5, zorder=6, label=f"threshold: water peak {WATER_MIN:g}")
    if show_fit and good:
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore", RuntimeWarning)
            mean_good = np.nanmean(good, axis=0)
        p = fit_two_gaussians(mean_good)
        ratio = water_fat(mean_good)
        x = np.linspace(2, 25, 600)
        for (height, centre, sigma), colour in ((p[:3], FAT_COLOUR), (p[3:], WATER_COLOUR)):
            within = (x >= centre - 3 * sigma) & (x <= centre + 3 * sigma)
            ax.fill_between(x[within], gaussian(x[within], height, centre, sigma), color=colour, alpha=0.25, lw=0)
        ax.plot(x, two_gaussians(x, *p), color="red", ls="--", lw=1.4, zorder=5, label="fit to the usable scans")
        ax.set_title(f"{side}, {label}: {len(good)} of {len(records)} usable\nWater:Fat = {ratio:.2f}")
    else:
        ax.set_title(f"{side}, {label}: 0 of {len(records)} usable\nnot used")
    ax.set(xlabel="q (nm⁻¹)", xlim=(2, 25))
    ax.set_xticks([5, 10, 15, 20, 25])
    ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
    ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=5, loc="upper left")
    ax.set_box_aspect(1)

plt.rcParams["font.size"] = 7
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(9, 3.6), sharey=True)
sides = sorted(("LEFT", "RIGHT"), key=lambda side: found[example_nova, side][0] != "NORMAL")
plot_breast(axes[0], example_nova, sides[0], show_fit=True)
plot_breast(axes[1], example_nova, sides[1], show_fit=True)
plot_breast(axes[2], rejected_example[0], rejected_example[1], show_fit=False)
axes[0].set_ylabel("I(q), prepared")
axes[0].set_ylim(0, None)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
plt.rcParams["font.size"] = 10
```

```{python}
from clinical import dense_share, rule_groups
usable_results = rule_results(WATER_MIN, CENTRE_MIN)
rejected_results = rule_results(WATER_MIN, CENTRE_MIN, rejected=True)
every_results = rule_results(-np.inf, -np.inf)
def share(results):
    higher, total, _ = results["CANCER vs NORMAL"]
    return f"{higher}/{total} ({higher / total:.0%})"
def ci(results):
    higher, total, _ = results["CANCER vs NORMAL"]
    interval = binomtest(higher, total).proportion_ci(method="exact")
    return f"{interval.low:.0%}–{interval.high:.0%}"
def p_value(results):
    return f"{results['CANCER vs NORMAL'][2]:.2g}"
usable_share = np.mean([usable(h, c, WATER_MIN, CENTRE_MIN) for *_, h, c in scan_records])
```

This fixed threshold is for **single-point** Human 1.0 scans, when only a few beams are placed. It is also the natural **stopgap** on Human 1.0
while mapping is not yet available (@sec-mapping): apply the same check during scanning and only keep a position if the short look is water-rich.
Chapter 1 (@sec-water-rich) makes the same “wet = information” point with a top/bottom `{python} PART`% cut, which is the natural rule once a
whole breast is mapped.

@fig-usable-rejected applies the threshold to every breast: rejected (fatty) scans look the same for all three labels; usable scans are wetter
for BENIGN and CANCER than for NORMAL, with BENIGN and CANCER almost the same under this cut. The paired comparison that works is CANCER vs
NORMAL (@sec-glandular-details).

```{python}

together = np.vstack([np.vstack(c) for c in list(rejected_by_label.values()) + list(usable_by_label.values()) if c])
covered = np.flatnonzero(np.isfinite(together).all(axis=0))
columns = slice(covered[0], covered[-1] + 1)
mean_water = {}

plt.rcParams["font.size"] = 7
fig, (rej_ax, use_ax) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(8, 3.8), sharey=True)
for ax, curves_by_label, title in ((rej_ax, rejected_by_label, "Rejected scans"), (use_ax, usable_by_label, "Usable, water-rich scans")):
    ax.set_box_aspect(1)

        stack = np.vstack(curves_by_label[label])

        colour = ne.STATUS_COLOURS[label]

    ax.set(title=title, xlabel="q (nm⁻¹)", xlim=(2, q[columns][-1]))
```

## Before and after

The same paired comparison, one number per patient, using every scan, then only the usable scans, then only the rejected ones:

| Scans used | CANCER breast higher | 95% CI | p (binomial, against 50%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Every scan (before) | `{python} share(every_results)` | `{python} ci(every_results)` | `{python} p_value(every_results)` |
| **Usable scans (after)** | **`{python} share(usable_results)`** | **`{python} ci(usable_results)`** | **`{python} p_value(usable_results)`** |
| Rejected scans | `{python} share(rejected_results)` | `{python} ci(rejected_results)` | `{python} p_value(rejected_results)` |

Using every scan, the CANCER breast is already the wetter one in most patients, but the fatty scans dilute the signal. Taking them out raises the
share to `{python} share(usable_results)`; the fatty scans on their own are at chance. The rule accepts
`{python} f"{usable_share:.0%}"` of all scans. Every patient with both breasts usable under this rule is plotted in @sec-usable-patients. Further
checks on the threshold and who is left out are in @sec-glandular-details.

## Who the rule compares

As in @sec-water-rich, denser tissue is where the signal is. Under this rule the patients compared are mostly BI-RADS C or D:
**`{python} f"{dense_share['compared']:.0%}"`** of `{python} len(rule_groups['compared'])`, against
`{python} f"{dense_share['left out']:.0%}"` of the `{python} len(rule_groups['left out'])` left out (@fig-who-left-out).
